title: Credit card band karne ko bola, bank 7 din mein band nahi kare toh roz ₹500 milega?
hooks: Credit card band karne ko bola, bank 7 din mein band nahi kare toh roz ₹500 milega
Bank credit card band nahi kar raha? RBI ke niyam se roz ₹500 penalty milti hai
7 working days mein card band nahi hua toh bank se ₹500 roz lene ka tarika
hook_why: Opens with the exact ₹ number the viewer gets (₹500/day) and the trigger condition (7 working days), matching the 'Bank pays you' hook pattern that won on rival reels. No greeting, no setup — the surprise is in the first 6 words.
metaphor: A ticking timer on a credit card that turns green (money to you) when the bank crosses the 7-working-day line
mechanism: Customer clears all dues and submits closure request via app/email/IVR
Bank has 7 working days to close the card and confirm via SMS/email
If bank misses deadline, ₹500/day penalty auto-starts from day 8
Customer keeps request proof (ticket number, date) and escalates to bank's nodal officer
If unresolved in 30 days, file on RBI CMS portal (cms.rbi.org.in) for compensation

caption:
Credit card band karne ko bola, bank 7 din mein band nahi kare toh roz ₹500 milega?

Zero outstanding hai toh 7 working days ka rule lagta hai. Request ka screenshot, ticket number, date — sab save rakho. Bank na mane toh nodal officer → RBI CMS portal.

Tumne kabhi card closure ke liye penalty claim kiya? Comment mein batao.

Source: RBI Master Direction · 21 Apr 2022
Save karo, kaam aayega 📌

claims.claim: RBI Master Direction dated 21 April 2022 mandates credit card closure within 7 working days of request
claims.basis: RBI Master Direction on Credit Card and Debit Card — Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022 (dated 21 Apr 2022), confirmed by LiveMint, Times Now Hindi, Asianet News

claims.claim: Penalty of ₹500 per day applies from the 8th working day if card not closed and zero outstanding balance
claims.basis: Same RBI Master Direction; LiveMint article 'बैंक नहीं बंद कर रहा क्रेडिट कार्ड? हर दिन मिलेगा ₹500'; Times Now Hindi 'Credit Card Close Rule: 7 Din Mein Card Band Nahi Hua To Bank...'; Asianet News 'Credit Card: 7 दिन में कार्ड बंद न होने पर बैंक देगा ₹500 रोज'

claims.claim: Penalty only applies when no outstanding dues (zero balance, no EMI, no unbilled charges) on the card
claims.basis: All cited news sources explicitly state condition: 'sirf jab koi outstanding na ho', 'agar aapke card par koi pending dues nahi hai', 'sara bill jama kar diya ho'

claims.claim: Customer can escalate to bank's principal nodal officer, then RBI CMS portal (cms.rbi.org.in) after 30 days
claims.basis: LiveMint: 'sabse pehle bank ke pradhan nodal adhikari ke paas shikayat darj karein... 30 din mein jawab na mile toh RBI lokpal ke paas'; Times Now Hindi: 'cms.rbi.org.in par jaakar online shikayat darj karayein'

claims.claim: Real case: bank paid ₹3.21 lakh compensation for months of delay in closing card
claims.basis: LiveMint and Asianet News both report the same case: 'haal hi mein ek mamle mein bank ne mahino tak card band nahi kiya... ₹3.21 lakh ka muavza dena pada'

fresh_fixed: scene 2: The message text uses '10-Nov-2026' which is fine, but the script implies the user is just now discovering the rule. The logic is generally sound, but the prompt requires checking against current facts. The script is accurate regarding the 7 working days rule.

scene 3: The script mentions 'RBI Master Direction' as the rule source. This is correct per the 21 April 2022 RBI Master Direction on Credit Card and Debit Card – Issuance and Conduct Directions, which is still the governing document as of Nov 2026.

scene 4: The script claims '10 din late = ₹5,000'. The RBI rule says '₹500 per day' after the 7 working days. If the bank is 10 days late *beyond* the 7 working days, that is 10 days of penalty. The math is correct based on the rule. No error found.
scene 7: The script suggests 'cms.rbi.org.in' for complaints. This is the correct current portal for the Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS).

steps_learned: Initiate closure request via the bank's app.
Ensure the credit card has zero outstanding balance and no EMIs.
Wait for the bank to process the request within 7 working days.
If the bank fails to close it within 7 working days, they are liable to pay ₹500 per day penalty.
If the bank delays, contact the nodal officer, then file a complaint on the RBI CMS portal.
missing_steps: The script does not mention that the online closure option is mandatory for banks (as per Equis.in), which is a key actionable step if the app doesn't show it.
It fails to explain how to prove the request date (e.g., saving the acknowledgment email or reference number), which is crucial for claiming the penalty.
It doesn't explain the CIBIL impact of closing an old credit card, which is a significant consideration mentioned in the source.
unsourced: The claim '10 din late = ₹5,000' is mathematically correct based on the rule, but the script presents it as a guaranteed outcome without mentioning the need for proof or escalation, which might mislead users into thinking it's automatic.
